lead: Frisco plumbing deals with clay soil, post-tension slabs and a city of mostly new homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Frisco.
risk: slab leaks in shifting clay, water heater and tankless upkeep, and irrigation backflow testing
risk_short: slab leaks, water heaters and backflow
why: Most Frisco homes were built after 2000 on post-tension slabs over expansive clay. Clay movement in drought and heavy rain can still stress supply lines under the floor.
Many homes have tankless heaters, softeners and sprinkler systems. Texas rules require backflow devices on irrigation systems, and many need testing.
utility: City of Frisco Public Works (water from the North Texas Municipal Water District)
water: Frisco buys treated water from the North Texas Municipal Water District, which draws largely from Lavon Lake. The water is moderately hard.
tips: Water your foundation evenly in dry summers.
Never cut into a post-tension slab without a plumber's scan.
areas: PipeMend works in Stonebriar, Starwood, Phillips Creek Ranch, Newman Village, Richwoods, the Grove, Downtown Frisco and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Frisco Building Inspections Division, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Why are post-tension slabs a plumbing concern in Frisco?
faq.a: Post-tension slabs hold steel cables under high tension. Cutting into one to reach a pipe can be dangerous. A plumber locates the cables first, or reroutes the line overhead instead.
